summary: The PR removes the check for `user.address` in `getUserCity`, causing a `TypeError` when a user object without an `address` property (or with a `null`/`undefined` address) is passed to the function.

findings.title: Uncaught TypeError when user.address is missing or null
findings.description: Removing the guard `if (!user.address) return null;` causes `getUserCity` to attempt accessing `user.address.city` directly. If `user.address` is `undefined` or `null`, Node.js will throw an unhandled `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'city')` instead of returning `null` or gracefully handling missing address information.
findings.verificationHypothesis: Calling `getUserCity({ name: 'Alice' })` or `getUserCity({ address: null })` will throw a TypeError instead of returning `null` or `undefined`.

suggestedReproduction.preconditions: The user object passed to getUserCity does not have an address property defined.
suggestedReproduction.expectedBehavior: The function should return null or undefined gracefully when user.address is missing.
suggestedReproduction.suspiciousBehavior: The function throws an unhandled TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'city').
